The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T09:34:00Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-12T09:34:02Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came 6 minutes {detection_gap} after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
Broken from 2026-11-12T09:27:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-12T09:35:00Z {back_to_normal}, when the metrics show it back to normal.
That is 8 minutes {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 2 minutes 6 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T09:36:08Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 1.0% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 26.3% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 39.0% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 25.3% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 1.0333333333333333% {series_before} before it began, 26.3125% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 39% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 4,714.52 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-12T09:34:02Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-12T09:34:03Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-12T09:34:03Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-12T09:34:04Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 09:34 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-12T09:34:04Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 361 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-12T09:34:04Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 09:27 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-12T09:34:04Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-12T09:34:07Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 12 09:28 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-12T09:34:07Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-12T09:34:07Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-12T09:34:07Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 37 {T11.2} minutes before 09:34 {T11.3}
  - [T12] 2026-11-12T09:34:07Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 142 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-12T09:34:11Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-12T09:34:11Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-12T09:34:11Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 09:34:11 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-12T09:34:11Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-12T09:34:11Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-12T09:34:12Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C1, moved from OFF to ON
  - [T19] 2026-11-12T09:34:13Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 09:35 {T19.2} - up to 167s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-12T09:36:08Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 09:34 {T20.2}
  - [T21] 2026-11-12T09:36:08Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
  - [T22] 2026-11-12T09:36:08Z {T22.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATED - set flag [legacy-checkout-fallback] ON and the rule that fired stopped firing
  - [T23] 2026-11-12T09:36:58Z {T23.1} Code-Fix Agent: Proposed a fix as a draft pull request - https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/569

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-12T09:27:52Z {P1.1} flag-toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G153f] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=on - 200 {G153f.1} evaluations - 30 {G153f.2} occurrences in 30 {G153f.3} minutes, 08:57–09:26 {G153f.4}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 50 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 30 {G46bc.2} minutes, 08:57–09:26 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 37 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 38 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 08:57–09:34 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 39.00% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 09:31 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 1 {Gad41.1} occurrence in 1 {Gad41.2} minute, 09:22 {Gad41.3}
  - [G7ad6] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 20 {G7ad6.1} / on 180 {G7ad6.2} - 200 {G7ad6.3} evaluations - 1 {G7ad6.4} occurrence in 1 {G7ad6.5} minute, 09:27 {G7ad6.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 16 {G5309.1} occurrences in 8 {G5309.2} minutes, 09:27–09:34 {G5309.3}
  - [G7037] INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 {G7037.1} evaluations - 7 {G7037.2} occurrences in 7 {G7037.3} minutes, 09:28–09:34 {G7037.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched from on to off at 2026-11-12T09:27:52Z {C1.1}. Account page requests then began failing with ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to about 33% {C1.3}. No deployment was involved. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.9 {C1.4}, confirmed]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for [C1] (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix, and what it claims is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [F1] `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py worked out `account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)`. `bought_this_month` holds only the purchases marked `in_current_month`, so it is empty for any shopper who has bought before but not this month. That is an ordinary shopper, not an edge case: the test file's own builder `an_account_with_no_purchases_this_month` calls it "the ordinary case". For every such account the function raised ZeroDivisionError at line 47 {F1.1}. `render_spend_summary` lets that reach `serve_account_page`, which records it as a failed page. So any request sent down the monthly path (`use_monthly_summary=True`) failed for these shoppers. This is the path the flag change opened up.
      
      The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0 {F1.2}. That is the correct average spend this month for a shopper who spent nothing (their `total_this_month_cents` is 0 {F1.3}). Nothing else changes. The lifetime average and the typical-spend path are untouched. A real failure still propagates as before: an account with no purchases at all still raises from `average_spend_per_item`, and the existing test that checks this is kept.
      
      The new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py are written to show two things. First, the monthly average is 0 {F1.4} for a shopper with past purchases but none this month. Second, `render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True)` returns 0 {F1.5} for that shopper rather than raising. Both cases raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code. That makes the page safe with the flag in either state.
  - Say what the files Code-Fix read do, with the conditions it gives - a default as a default, never as all it does - and no wider: 'nothing in the files it read', never 'nothing in the code'.

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, done): Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback
  - AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix
PR #569 is a draft Argus opened for a person to review and merge. The record holds nothing about it after that: do not say it was reviewed, approved or merged, or that it was not - nor that the record holds nothing, which the document says itself. Nothing ran its test or its fix: say what it proposes, not that it corrects anything.
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1].

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages take the monthly spend-summary path. There, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and nothing guards against that number being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, which `render_spend_summary` passes up to `serve_account_page`, and the page is recorded as failed. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month.
still_at_risk: If legacy-checkout-fallback is switched off again, account pages can fail again for shoppers who have past purchases but none this month.
symptom: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The account page requests failed because rendering them raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appear in the onset minute. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: The division by zero began when admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off at {P1.1}. Before that, every evaluation read the flag as on and account pages rendered normally. Evaluations started reading off in the minute of the change and read off in every minute after it. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G153f, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7ad6, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7037, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour before {T15.4}, and that change was this one. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order"; P1, under "Changes to production it read")
causal_chain 4: With the flag off, account pages likely take the monthly spend-summary path, which divides by the number of items bought this month, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month. (cites F1, under "What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed, in Code-Fix's words - nothing ran its test or its fix")
contributing_factors 1: The flag change reached all of io-shop's traffic within the minute it was made. No staged rollout and no check before the change was seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout with a check on the error rate would have shown the failures on a small share of requests and stopped the change before it reached most shoppers.
contributing_factors 2: No test was seen that runs the account page with legacy-checkout-fallback off for a shopper who has past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's new tests for that case raise against the current code.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero on the monthly path would have been caught before the path was ever turned on in production.
contributing_factors 3: The HighErrorRate rule waits {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires, so the error rate stayed high for some time before anything acted on it.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: With a shorter hold, the alert, and so the flag revert, would have come sooner, and the incident would have been shorter.
action_items 1: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, and roll them back automatically if the error rate rises.
action_items 2: Run io-shop's test suite in CI with each feature flag in both states, so a code path a flag opens is tested before the flag can be changed.
action_items 3: Review whether the HighErrorRate rule on io-shop can fire with a shorter hold without becoming noisy.
action_items 4: Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so a person is paged when it fires.
action_items 5: Lock legacy-checkout-fallback ON against further changes until the fix in PR #569 is merged.
went_wrong 1: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in to respond.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
